column1: # How people type Nepali in Latin letters in a chat, and what they mean by it.
# Two kinds of spelling are here that the Nepali phonetic rules cannot reach:
#  - Words the rules get wrong because Latin spelling does not carry the
#    difference: a long vowel nobody doubles ("ramro" is राम्रो, "kura" is
#    कुरा), the nasal nobody types ("kaha" is कहाँ, "naya" is नयाँ), dental
#    against retroflex ("thulo" is ठूलो), the short closing vowel of a
#  - Chat shorthand and the corpus's own habits: "xa" and "cha" for छ, "v" for
#    भ ("vayo", "vanda"), "k" for के, "hjr" for हजुर, "px" for पछि.
# Words the rules already spell right (गर्छ, हुन्छ, घरमा, रामलाई) are left
# out. Every form was checked against the Nepali word list, and where the list
# spells a word two ways the commoner spelling is used (काठमाडौँ, तपाईँ).
# Format: spelling<TAB>Nepali, one per line, lowercase keys.
